seo_title: Allahabad HC: Noida Allottee Gets Zero-Period Benefit
title: Allahabad High Court Grants Zero-Period Benefit From Original Allotment Date to Noida Commercial Plot Buyer
case_name: M/s Aloft Solutions Pvt. Ltd. v. State of U.P. and 3 Others
citation: Writ-C No. 30566 of 2025; Division Bench judgment dated 12 November 2026 (Varma and Singh, JJ.; reserved 9 October 2026)
card_summary: Aloft Solutions was allotted a commercial plot in Sector 43, Noida, in July 2007, but a status quo order in separate litigation over the same sector kept the plot undeveloped for years. The Allahabad High Court held NOIDA's conduct did not justify denying zero-period benefit from the allotment date, directed the payment schedule recalculated accordingly, and ordered possession within two weeks of a certified copy.
card_tip: A Noida allottee kept out of a plot by a status quo order passed in someone else's litigation can seek zero-period relief running back to the allotment date, not merely from when the status quo began.
verification_notes: The writ number (Writ-C No. 30566 of 2025), the bench (Siddhartha Varma and Kunal Ravi Singh, JJ.), the reserved date (9 October 2026), the pronouncement date (12 November 2026), the plot description (Plot No. A-146/2, Block-A, Sector 43, Noida, allotted 27 July 2007) and the operative directions (zero-period recalculation and two-week possession) were read from the judgment text reproduced at the first source, which is a near-primary reproduction of the order, and summarised consistently at the second source. Both sources are hosted on the same aggregator (SupremeToday); despite two separate targeted searches in this run, no independent reporter (LiveLaw, Bar and Bench, or local Noida press) covering this specific writ was found, so this limitation is flagged rather than concealed. The underlying Kendriya Karamchari Sahkari Greh Nirman Samiti litigation that produced the status quo order was not independently opened; the card states only that such litigation existed, as recited in the judgment.
